knowledge_point: There are two ways to mark NPs with locative =ko [cf.][]huber2018. When there is no ambiguity with regard to the location of the referent, or when the location is big or generic, =ko can be attached to a NP consisting of just a noun. This applies to place namesnames!place names (see [ref]), landscape features such as kolak `forest; mountain; mainland' or pasier `sea' (see [ref]) and kewe `house' (see [ref]). With smaller and more specific nouns, like bakul `basket' (see [ref]) or kaden `body' (see [ref]), the exact location has to be specified with the help of a relational noun. These nouns are commonly inflected with possessive suffix -un and and then followed by locative =ko (see Table~[ref] in §[ref]).
